title: Meat Suit or The Shitshow of Motherhood by Aya Ogawa at Second Stage ...
transcript: Motherhood is a shit show. But don't just take it from me, a childless man in his twenties. Within the first ten minutes of Aya Ogawa's new play, you will concur. There's not a central plot to this piece, it's more like a series of distinct scenes, almost all of which are about motherhood. It explores postpartum depression, how motherhood can reshape your identity, and the competitive nature of parenting, just to list a few. This play is comedically candid, and the aesthetic is wonderfully absurd. The costuming in particular is hilarious and heavily integrated into the storytelling in a really cool way that blends standard costuming, prop work, and puppetry. The whole thing is quite the roller coaster — I was humored, I was touched, and I could tell that it resonated with a lot of the audience. The ideas here aren't necessarily new, but there seem to be few other theatre pieces that have tackled them so head-on and in such a creative way. The material was actually derived from and inspired by interviews with real mothers, so there's almost a subtle documentary aspect to the piece which I think is pretty cool. My overall impression of the piece, though, was definitely a mixed bag. The ordering of the scenes doesn't always make sense, and I think that makes the tone of the play feel inconsistent. It also frays a little too much in thematic scope, devolving from a sharp examination of motherhood into an unwieldy exploration of life and death by the end of it. There's certainly good stuff in here — I just think some restructuring and trimming would have allowed it to pack more of a punch. With that, another program for my collection.
